ai_summary: Great Britain's electricity system is currently seeing 12.7 GW of GB wind output, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 4.5 GW, representing 44.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this clean generation, Scottish carbon intensity sits at an exceptional 0 gCO2/kWh versus 93 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, due to severe north-south grid bottlenecks, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 44.5 GWh. Turning down this low-cost generation through Balancing Mechanism bids has accrued a constraint cost of about £1,882,573 today alone. Extrapolating this daily constraint spend yields an estimated total yearly cost of £687 million, which is estimated to increase everybody's invoice in the UK by approximately £2 to £3/MWh when socialised across typical national demand. Furthermore, replacing this lost zero-carbon power required an estimated 8,458,249 m3 of gas burned elsewhere on the network, discharging an additional 15,581 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. This ongoing curtailment and substitute thermal dispatch demonstrate how transmission bottlenecks inflate consumer electricity bills and dilute national decarbonisation gains despite abundant renewable energy availability.
